title: Signal Bridge Collector and Compact Ingest Protocol (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc proposes the 'Signal Bridge' lightweight collector and an accompanying Compact Ingest Protocol (CIP) for shipping control evidence to the central evidence indexer and SIEM export pipeline. Goal is lower runtime footprint for edge collectors, predictable audit schema, improved deduping & provenance, and compatibility with RBAC v2 controls for access & signing keys.

Background / Problem space:
- Current evidence harvesters are heavyweight and assume always-on network and large local storage. Causes delays in environments with intermittent connectivity and increases PII exposure surface.
- Multiple teams have divergent JSON field shapes for audit events; downstream SIEM exports require brittle mappings.
- We need a small, signed, checkpoint-friendly envelope that can be uploaded to the evidence store or queued for SIEM export with minimal transformation.

Design goals (summary):
- Compact canonical envelope for evidence (CIP) with predictable fields and optional binary attachments encoded as chunked base64+manifest.
- Collector runs as a tiny sidecar (single binary ~15MB), limited dependencies, TLS + signing with short-lived keys from RBAC v2 KMS flow.
- Checkpointing: per-collector sequence numbers + cryptographic anchors for tamper detection.
- Deduping hints and TTLs to minimize storage & SIEM noise.
- Export mapping (one-to-one) to SIEM neutral fields (CEF/LEEF/syslog) and to internal audit_log_v2 schema.

Compact Ingest Protocol (CIP) envelope (field definitions):
- version: string (e.g., "1.0")
- collector_id: string (uuid) - stable id assigned at install time
- seq: string (monotonic integer as string) - resets on re-install, combined with collector_id for ordering
- ts_utc: string (ISO8601) - event capture time in UTC
- event_type: string (e.g., CONTROL_CHANGE, ACCESS_GRANT, DEPLOYMENT, ERROR, HEARTBEAT)
- actor: string (short principal id, e.g., service:deploy-api or user:liam.chen@redwood.com)
- actor_role: string (role name from RBAC v2)
- space: string (logical boundary e.g., org:acme-prod or internal:infra)
- target: string (resource id, e.g., model:llama-70b-prod/variantA)
- action: string (allowed values: CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE, READ, EXECUTE, AUTHZ_CHANGE)
- payload_checksum: string (sha256 hex of payload bytes, optional if payload_size==0)
- payload_size: string (bytes, as string)
- payload_encoding: string (raw | base64-chunked | external-ref)
- payload_manifest: string (if base64-chunked, JSON list encoded as base64 of {chunk_id, order, size})
- attachments: string (optional list of attachment descriptors as base64 JSON)
- provenance_anchor: string (sha256 hex combining collector_id|seq|ts_utc|payload_checksum)
- signature: string (compact ed25519 signature over canonicalized minimal envelope fields)
- metadata: string (optional freeform tags as comma-separated k=v pairs)

Notes about field types: CIP intentionally represents numeric fields as strings to avoid cross-language/locale parsing edge cases in small collectors (JS, Go, Rust).

Sample CIP (line-delimited simplified representation):
{"version":"1.0","collector_id":"c8f4e2a2-0b1a-4a9f-9a6f-2f1a9e8d7b5c","seq":"1024","ts_utc":"2025-03-04T21:14:03Z","event_type":"CONTROL_CHANGE","actor":"service:rollout-engine","actor_role":"platform-deploy","space":"org:redwood-prod","target":"route:api/v1/generate","action":"UPDATE","payload_checksum":"b1946ac92492d2347c6235b4d2611184","payload_size":"224","payload_encoding":"base64-chunked","provenance_anchor":"3f7b6c2a...","signature":"Zq3V...","metadata":"priority=high,region=us-west2"}
(note: actual payloads and chunks are uploaded separately or embedded depending on config)

Audit log v2 mapping (internal canonical fields):
- audit_id: generated by indexer as uuid (not in CIP)
- captured_at -> ts_utc
- principal_id -> actor
- principal_role -> actor_role
- resource -> target
- operation -> action
- change_summary -> derived from small text payload extracted by indexer (max 2KB)
- raw_blob_ref -> pointer to payload or attachment stored in object store
- provenance_hash -> provenance_anchor
- ingest_source -> collector_id
- ingest_seq -> seq
- retention_class -> derived from space+event_type (see retention table below)

Retention classes (recommended):
- CLASS_A (compliance-critical): CONTROL_CHANGE, AUTHZ_CHANGE, high priority ACCESS_GRANT -> 7 years
- CLASS_B (operational): DEPLOYMENT, SERVICE_CONFIG -> 2 years
- CLASS_C (transient): HEARTBEAT, METRIC_SAMPLE, DEBUG -> 90 days

RBAC v2 integration (key flows and roles):
- Collector installation uses short-lived install token minted by onboarding flow. Token tied to installer principal (user or infra) and scoped to 'collector:install' permission for a single org/space.
- Once installed, collector requests a signer cert from KMS service using its collector_id and install token. RBAC v2 policy enforces: signer:create scoped to {collector_id, space}.
- Signer keys rotate every 24h by default; collectors reconcile and prefetch new certs when token TTL < 30 minutes.
- Required RBAC roles for reading evidence in the indexer: evidence-reader, evidence-auditor (read + export), evidence-admin (read/write/manage retention).
- SIEM export role mapping: only principals with evidence-auditor or evidence-admin can enable SIEM exports for a space.

Collector implementation notes (operational):
- Runtime: Go preferred for minimal binary and static linking. Single-process, non-root.
- Storage: circular buffer on disk, configurable max_bytes (default 128MB). Older checkpoints trimmed after successful index ack.
- Network: TLS1.3 with mutual TLS to indexer when available; fallback to signed uploads to object-store when MTLS unavailable.
- Buffering strategy: exponential backoff with bounded retry queue size and per-record retry metadata.
- Checkpoint protocol: indexer returns (collector_id, seq_ack) when it has persisted up to seq N. Collectors compact and drop local data <= seq_ack.
- Offline signing: collector must keep last two signer keys to re-sign if required during replay windows.

SIEM export mapping and conversion rules:
- We produce two export formats: LEEF/CEF (legacy) and JSON ECS-compatible (preferred).
- Mapping highlights (CIP -> ECS):
  - event.created -> ts_utc
  - user.id -> actor
  - user.roles -> actor_role (comma-separated -> array in ECS)
  - event.action -> action
  - file.hash.sha256 -> payload_checksum (if attachment is file)
  - url.original -> raw_blob_ref when payload is external URL
  - host.hostname -> collector_id (mapped as host.id if collector runs on host)
  - message -> compact change_summary
- Enrichers: add geoip for collector_id IP, add org metadata from space tag.
- Rate limiting: max 500 events/sec per space to SIEM export (configurable feature flag). Backpressure from SIEM should cause indexer to buffer and batch by time-window (default 5s).

Deduping strategy:
- Primary dedupe key = provenance_anchor. If collision, compare payload_checksum and actor+ts_utc.
- Collectors include 'duplicate_hint' boolean when they detect local duplicates to speed downstream deduping. Indexer persists a small bloom filter per space for recent anchors to avoid re-ingesting duplicates for a rolling 7-day window.

Chain-of-custody and preservation:
- Each CIP envelope includes provenance_anchor and signature. Indexer stores signature and the canonicalized minimal envelope used to verify signature at ingest time.
- Proof-of-preservation document generated per ingest window (daily) that contains short Merkle root of the day's anchors and is signed with the indexer root key. This aids future forensics and legal holds.

Failure modes & mitigations:
- Lost or corrupted local storage: collector replays from last known remote ack; if ack unknown, collector can present local checkpoint and request a 'trust-reset' flow that requires platform-ops approval.
- Stalled signer rotation: collectors continue to sign with last valid key for a replay window (configurable, default 48h) but emit an alert and increment health metric 'signer_stale'.
- SIEM endpoint backpressure: indexer switches to store-and-export-later and marks space as 'export-delayed' with alerting.

Testing checklist (pre-rollout):
- [ ] Unit tests for signature verification, provenance anchor computation, checkpointing logic.
- [ ] Fuzz test CIP canonicalization across languages (Go, Node).
- [ ] Integration: collector <-> indexer mtls + signed upload fallback tested in simulated flaky network.
- [ ] SIEM mapping verification with Splunk (CEF) and Elastic ECS mapping.
- [ ] Retention enforcement tests (CLASS_A delete checks require two-step auth).

Rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0 (canary): Deploy Signal Bridge collector to internal infra projects (2 hosts) and enable CIP ingestion to a non-prod indexer. Duration: 2 weeks.
- Phase 1 (pilot): Select 3 customer-facing spaces with low-volume control-change events; enable SIEM export to test aggregation. Duration: 4 weeks.
- Phase 2 (gradual): Increase to 25% of spaces, tune dedupe bloom filter and retention mapping. Duration: 6 weeks.
- Phase 3 (GA): Turn on default in new installs and offer migration tooling for legacy harvesters.

Operational runbook pointers (quick):
- collector-health metrics: collector_uptime, seq_lag, signer_stale, local_buffer_bytes
- indexer metrics: ingest_latency_p50/p99, ack_seq_lag_by_collector, export_queue_size_by_space
- common recovery steps: rotate signer (admin CLI), trigger trust-reset (requires SRE manual approval), replay from archive (object-store)

Open questions & decisions needed:
- Default signer rotation interval: 24h vs 12h (security vs reliability).
- Bloom filter sizing: memory tradeoff vs dedupe accuracy; propose 4MB per active space (tunable).
- Will we allow attachments in raw (embedded) form for CLASS_A events? (PII risk)

Appendix A — Example CLI flows:
- Install: redwood-collector install --org acme-prod --space api --token <install-token>
- Checkpoint query: redwood-collector status --collector-id <id> -> returns seq,last-ack
- Manual replay: redwood-collector replay --from-seq 1000 --to-seq 1200 --target indexer-staging

Appendix B — Short glossary:
- CIP: Compact Ingest Protocol (this doc)
- indexer: central evidence ingestion and indexing service
- provenance_anchor: compact integrity fingerprint for each envelope

Notes: This is a working draft intended to capture the minimal viable collector and ingest format that satisfies our compliance, forensics, and SIEM export needs. Feedback welcome — prefer concrete tradeoffs (numbers) rather than high-level statements.
